data.claim: Yes: _counts_as_mine matches holder==me whatever tree the lease is bound to, so an agent holding two items covers tree A's commits with item B's files and 'You hold' lists B's globs

data.question: Does the commit hook count every lease of the committing identity as covering a commit in one item's tree?

chunk_findings.detail: The fix only stops a same-holder/different-tree lease from being treated as “mine” when `bound` is True. `_tree_bound` is True only if `here` is the worktree of a live, unfinished lease. So if the commit happens in a tree whose own lease has lapsed (and is therefore absent from `unfinished_leases`), `bound` is False and the old bug remains: a live lease I hold for a different worktree still counts as mine by holder match. Concrete input: live lease B has `holder == me`, `worktree = W_B`, `globs = ["b/**"]`; commit runs in lapsed tree `W_A` touching `b/file.py`. `_tree_bound(W_A)` returns False, `_counts_as_mine(B)` returns True, so `_split_leases` puts `b/**` in `mine`, and the hook allows/lists B’s globs from the wrong tree. The same failure also occurs for any non-live owned tree, such as a main checkout not represented in `unfinished_leases`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_counts_as_mine

chunk_findings.detail: The hook now computes `bound = _tree_bound(...)` and passes it to `_split_leases` and `_with_contested`, but the `_expired_you_hold` call below the shown hunk is unchanged and still uses the new parameter’s default `False`. As a result, the lapsed-lease path does not apply the new classification: when `here` is bound to a live lease, a lapsed lease I hold for a *different* tree can still be reported as “would have been mine” / “claim X” using the old holder-only test, even though the added parameter exists precisely to apply the same bound-aware test there.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_expired_you_hold

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `E.check_commit(repo, cfg, agent="owner") == (0, "")` when T1 is bound to the current worktree with glob `src/*`, and the same holder also has T2 with no worktree leasing `docs/x.md`. That preserves the bug this change is meant to fix: the commit is in T1's tree, so the hook must judge it by T1's lease, and T2 is still "another item of the same holder"—its no-tree lease should not cover a different item's tree. If the implementation satisfies this assertion by treating an empty tree bound as matching every tree, then Bc57d0b031a still occurs whenever the committing agent also holds an additional no-tree item whose glob matches the edited path. The no-tree fallback is only defensible when the current checkout is not some other item's tree (the third test), not when it is T1's tree.
